statement: Lena bikes $24$ kilometers to a lake at an average speed of $12$ kilometers per hour. She returns along the same route at an average speed of $8$ kilometers per hour. What is her average speed, in kilometers per hour, for the whole round trip?

choices.misconception: I divided the one-way distance of 24 km by the total time of 5 hours, forgetting she rode 48 km in all.
I averaged the two speeds, 12 and 8, but she spends more time at the slower speed, so that simple average is too high.
I divided the total distance of 48 km by only the 3 hours of the return trip.

hints: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.
Find the time for each leg by dividing distance by speed, add the times, then divide the total distance by the total time.
The trip out takes $24 \div 12 = 2$ hours and the trip back takes $24 \div 8 = 3$ hours, so she rides 48 km in 5 hours.

solutions.reliable: Going: $24 \div 12 = 2$ hours. Returning: $24 \div 8 = 3$ hours. The total distance is $48$ km and the total time is $5$ hours, so the average speed is $48 \div 5 = 9.6$ km/h. The idea: average speed is total distance over total time, not the average of the speeds, because the slower leg lasts longer.
solutions.elegant: For two legs of equal distance, the average speed is the harmonic mean of the speeds: $\dfrac{2 \cdot 12 \cdot 8}{12 + 8} = \dfrac{192}{20} = 9.6$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
